builder_reading: Section 17 section 2 calls Operationally verified evidence "applicable". Each requirement has a required level; every rung up to that level is mandatory; higher rungs may be left out.
effect_if_wrong: Affects requirement closure evidence: a requirement could be closed on fewer rungs than the auditor intends.

builder_reading: The role names product_owner, spec_approver, authorised_reviewer, closure_authority, authority_owner, materiality_owner, policy_reviewer and finance_reviewer are placeholders.
effect_if_wrong: Affects the mapping to the real platform roles; every check keyed on a role name must be re-mapped.
auditor_note: Auditor: affects the mapping to real platform roles.

builder_reading: The first policy is compared with a fail-safe baseline (no rules), so it counts as a loosening that needs two humans including the owner.
effect_if_wrong: The first policy could be activated with fewer approvers than intended.

builder_reading: The engine adds this reason code; the CR-02 model has no such reason.
effect_if_wrong: A downstream consumer may not expect the code.

builder_reading: Evidence for run-type statuses carries an artefact hash and names its tests; the exact form is the builder.
effect_if_wrong: The form of integrity metadata may not match what the auditor wants.

builder_reading: A row has an intrinsic outcome at intake (accepted, accepted_with_warnings, pending_reconciliation, quarantined, rejected) and an effective outcome after reconciliation. Rejected rows are never stored as records; they are kept as reject evidence with the reason.
effect_if_wrong: Reviewers may expect a different set of states or a different place for rejected rows.

topic: Exact duplicate delivery versus duplicate candidate
builder_reading: Two invoices are an exact duplicate delivery only if supplier and supplier invoice number match AND every business field is equal. Anything less (same details, different or missing invoice number) is a DUPLICATE_CANDIDATE held for a person. The lowest key is treated as the original so the result does not depend on arrival order.
effect_if_wrong: Too strict leaves real duplicates for people; too loose counts a repeat once when it was two events.

builder_reading: A second delivery with the same key and different content at the same or unknown revision is a conflict: the record becomes a quarantined marker that keeps every version, sorted so arrival order does not matter. A higher declared revision supersedes an open conflict. A lower revision is stale evidence, not an update.
effect_if_wrong: Different treatment of corrections could overwrite financial data or hide a conflict.

builder_reading: Fail-safe: any optional value that is missing and not declared tolerable blocks use of the record (CRITICAL_VALUE_MISSING). Material fields can never be declared tolerable. The tolerated list in the demonstration is illustrative.
effect_if_wrong: Too strict floods reviewers; too loose lets an unknown be treated as usable.

builder_reading: A secondary source that disagrees with the primary quarantines the primary. A secondary source that disagrees with itself holds the primary for a person. With no approved register nothing is authoritative.
effect_if_wrong: A different reading could let a disagreeing system pass or block more than intended.

builder_reading: Stable identifier, then a person-approved alias, then the exact full name with legal words kept, then resemblance, which only shows candidates and never chooses. SYN Metro Steel is not SYN Metro Steel Pty Ltd.
effect_if_wrong: A looser ladder risks a forced merge; a stricter one sends more to review.

builder_reading: A credit note is netted against its invoice only if the credit itself is trusted; otherwise the invoice is left out of the authoritative total. A reissue found by invoice-number pattern is lineage information only.
effect_if_wrong: Netting an untrusted credit would understate cost.

builder_reading: No built-in thresholds. A limit is configuration per use; with none configured the answer is cannot_assess, never fresh.
effect_if_wrong: A built-in limit would be an invented threshold.

builder_reading: Extracted values stay unverified until a person with the document_verifier role verifies them, tied to the document hash. Ambiguous readings offer candidates and are never chosen by software.
effect_if_wrong: A weaker rule would let an OCR guess drive a financial figure.

builder_reading: The reference runner uses three attempts and waits of 1, 2 and 4 seconds as configuration defaults. They are engineering defaults, not product decisions.
effect_if_wrong: Different bounds change load and delay, not correctness.

builder_reading: A delivery is identified by the file hash, the mapping version and the source name. The same bytes under another mapping version or from another source are a separate delivery.
effect_if_wrong: A different key would change what counts as a replay.

builder_reading: With no tolerance configured, amounts must be exactly equal (for example a retention receipt and its bank transaction). No tolerance value is chosen.
effect_if_wrong: A tolerance would let a near-miss count as evidence.

builder_reading: Forecast final cost is the actual cost up to the forecast date plus the cost to complete declared or derived at that date. Invoices dated after the forecast date are shown separately and are never added.
effect_if_wrong: Adding later actuals to a cost to complete that already expects them would count them twice.

builder_reading: Carrying cost is estimated from the as-of date to the expected release date on the funded share of the withheld balance. Cost already incurred is not estimated because no balance history is ingested. A release date that has passed with money still withheld gives cannot be assessed.
effect_if_wrong: A backward or flat estimate would state a cost that no evidence supports.

builder_reading: Secured revenue uses the variation register; when the contract summary disagrees, the figure is provisional and both numbers are listed. Submitted, disputed and rejected variations are never revenue.
effect_if_wrong: Using the summary instead would hide an approved variation, or count an unapproved one.

topic: Records that cannot be attributed to a project
builder_reading: A record whose project cannot be told appears as an unattributed exclusion on every project figure, so it cannot be missed. It is not added to any total.
effect_if_wrong: Dropping it would hide cost; adding it would count it on the wrong project.

topic: What a total of included records means
builder_reading: A cost, commitment or revenue total is the sum of the records that can be used. If any record is held, disputed or unknown the figure is provisional and lists it. Cannot be assessed is used only when no figure can be formed at all.
effect_if_wrong: Showing zero or hiding the total when one record is held would mislead in the other direction.

topic: M4 role names and separation of duties
builder_reading: The roles policy_owner, forecast_owner, retention_clerk and retention_approver are the builder's names, like I-2. Whoever proposes a policy cannot approve it; whoever runs a forecast cannot adopt it; approval, release and receipt of retention need the approver role and a human.
effect_if_wrong: Different names or weaker separation change who can make a figure authoritative or move retention between states.

builder_reading: Cost-to-cost is the only method implemented (recognised revenue is secured revenue times cost to date over forecast final cost). Selecting a method is a policy choice; with none selected there is no recognised margin.
effect_if_wrong: A different method (for example certified progress) gives a different recognised margin.

builder_reading: Every method, funded share and freshness limit in the demonstration policy is the builder's illustrative choice. The policy has no default for any open decision; an unset one gives cannot be assessed and names the decision.
effect_if_wrong: Treating the demonstration values as defaults would settle open decisions.

builder_reading: Three methods are offered as configuration: declared, budget less actual, and declared else budget less actual. A held declared line is never replaced by a budget figure. A budget already exceeded gives an unknown cost to complete, never a negative one.
effect_if_wrong: Falling back silently would hide a disputed estimate; a negative figure would understate cost.

builder_reading: Retention moves withheld, claimed, approved, released, received with a disputed side state, one evidenced event at a time. Released is not received; received needs a bank transaction of exactly that amount. A due date passing moves nothing and only raises a review flag.
effect_if_wrong: Promoting a state on a date would assert entitlement or cash that no one has evidenced.

builder_reading: The bridge splits the change in forecast margin into items that add up to it exactly. A newly counted record or a recorded reason explains an item; a method change, a changed amount or a blank reason does not. No materiality threshold is applied.
effect_if_wrong: A threshold would hide small unexplained movements; none is chosen.

builder_reading: Open commitment is the committed amount less what is invoiced, never below zero, with any overrun shown separately. Unapproved amendments are exposure, not commitment. Draft and cancelled orders are not commitments.
effect_if_wrong: Counting exposure as commitment would overstate the cost to come.

topic: M5 role names and separation of duties
builder_reading: The roles detection_policy_owner, detection_service, finding_reviewer, finding_owner and action_approver are the builder's names. Only a service identity ingests detection runs; only a human can confirm, dismiss, approve, resolve or supersede; the person who proposes an action cannot approve it.
effect_if_wrong: Different names or weaker separation change who can move a finding.

builder_reading: A condition is identified by rule, scope and subject. There is one finding per identity, however many runs see it; the same condition does not create a second alert.
effect_if_wrong: A different identity rule would merge or split findings and change what is notified.

topic: A run always says what it did
builder_reading: Every rule yields a run record with status evaluated, not_configured, disabled or cannot_assess. Silence is never the only answer, and a rule that did not run says nothing about its findings.
effect_if_wrong: Treating a missing run as a clean result would hide a gap.

topic: Amount labels and separate severity, urgency and confidence
builder_reading: An amount is labelled figure, record or estimate. A signal that cannot be quantified carries a reason and no amount. Severity, urgency and confidence are three values, not one score.
effect_if_wrong: A single score or an unlabelled amount would blur what is known.

builder_reading: Cost over budget, invoice over order and quote over reference use strictly exceeds, by exact cross-multiplication with no rounding. Other rules use the comparison in their description (at least, longer than, days left not more than the warning). A threshold at exactly its boundary is stated per rule in the tests.
effect_if_wrong: A different boundary changes whether a case exactly at the threshold is reported.

builder_reading: Detection can create a finding, update it, mark it seen and reopen a resolved or dismissed one only when the material-change digest differs. A decision made after a run is not undone by that run. No path leads to a realised saving; claim_realised refuses.
effect_if_wrong: Automatic reopening or resolution would let a rerun overrule a person.

topic: A finding that stops being detected
builder_reading: It is marked not re-detected with the date, and is never resolved automatically. A person decides.
effect_if_wrong: Auto-resolution would remove findings because data went missing.

builder_reading: Findings overlap when they share an overlap group, share evidence records, or a person linked them as a financial overlap. The portfolio reports lower and upper bounds per interpretation and never sums interpretations; dismissed and superseded findings are excluded.
effect_if_wrong: Summing overlapping findings would overstate the total.

builder_reading: Weeks are complete Monday-based weeks; the rule compares output per hour over the recent weeks with the baseline weeks at package level only. A fall of at least the configured amount is reported; its money value is labelled an estimate (hours beyond what the baseline rate needs, times the recent average recorded hourly rate) and is unquantified when rates are missing.
effect_if_wrong: Partial weeks, crew-level comparison or a different rate would change which cases are reported and the estimate.

builder_reading: Delay events that overlap for at least the configured days are reported with the days. The cost of holding the site is not estimated.
effect_if_wrong: An estimate would assume a critical path nobody has provided.

builder_reading: The severity of a split-order cluster follows the aggregate order value (value at stake). The amount is a record amount, not a loss.
effect_if_wrong: Treating it as a loss would overstate exposure.

builder_reading: A notification has a dedup key; the same key is sent once inside the suppression window; a repeat is sent again only for a new finding, a reopening, a severity increase, a status transition or material evidence. A failed delivery stays pending and visible.
effect_if_wrong: Different re-notify events change how many alerts a person receives.

builder_reading: R07 compares only pairs a person declared comparable. APG does not decide comparability in M5.
effect_if_wrong: Inferring pairs would compare unlike items and report false savings.

builder_reading: Every threshold and window in the demonstration detection policy is the builder's illustrative choice, or comes from test_thresholds.json where marked. None has product-owner approval.
effect_if_wrong: Treating them as defaults would settle open decisions.

builder_reading: The roles procurement_policy_owner and specification_owner approve the procurement policy and the specification register. A policy or register version is immutable; the person who proposes a version cannot approve it; an unapproved version still runs but the result says it is unapproved. There are no defaults: a missing parameter makes the rule report not_configured and name it.
effect_if_wrong: Other role names or a weaker approval would change who may set a limit; a default would settle an open decision.

builder_reading: An offer is comparable, comparable with adjustment, partly comparable, not comparable or unverified. A failure from any evidence (the catalogue or a reading) blocks. A pass needs a reading verified by someone other than the extractor, with a date. The unit must be verified, otherwise the offer is only partly comparable. A rescaled offer is shown but gets no purchase scenario.
effect_if_wrong: Lenient rules would let an unlike item rank; strict rules would exclude usable offers.

builder_reading: A ranking is definitive only with at least two offers, all comparable or comparable with adjustment, all current, landed cost complete, no unresolved critical international check, no substitution and no held supporting record. Anything short of that is indicative, including a partly comparable offer (the conservative choice). may_recommend is the only gate and human approval is always required.
effect_if_wrong: A less strict gate would let a recommendation pass when it should not (the M6 acceptance wording).

builder_reading: There are four decision classes (quote ranking, buy timing, benchmark, import costing), each with its own limit for a quote, an index and a rate. A stale quote is still an offer but cannot make a ranking definitive; an expired or not-yet-issued quote is historical only; no observation is unavailable, never fresh. The age equal to the limit is fresh.
effect_if_wrong: Different limits or boundaries change which offers can be definitive.

builder_reading: The rate is the latest on or before the as-of day, expressed as foreign units per AUD. An amount in AUD is the foreign amount divided by the rate, rounded half away from zero once per component. The supplier's stated rate is kept and never replaced; the divergence is stated in basis points of the stated amount against the reference conversion, and the tolerance is configuration.
effect_if_wrong: A different convention changes every foreign landed cost.

builder_reading: The delivery basis decides which components are included in the rate (delivered includes freight and handling; ex-works and FOB include none). Required components differ for domestic and international offers. Prices are compared on the tax basis the policy states (ex GST) and GST is not computed. Tier price is chosen by quantity. A unit conversion uses only a factor declared in the specification register (in millionths) and only when the offered unit is verified; with no declared conversion the units are incompatible and with an unverified unit the offer is only partly comparable.
effect_if_wrong: A different basis changes which offer is cheapest.

builder_reading: An order covers a demand when project, material and window match: orders from 180 days before the required date up to the as-of day with status committed or closed. Identical orders held as duplicate candidates are counted as possible, not confirmed. Surplus beyond 500 basis points is flagged. An order unit that differs from the demand unit is not converted: coverage is cannot_assess.
effect_if_wrong: A different window, status set or tolerance changes which orders count as cover.

builder_reading: Buy now orders on the as-of day. Wait orders on the latest day that still meets the required date after the lead time and its variation, with price paths only from the policy. Stage splits the quantity as the policy says with its extra delivery and admin costs. Storage and financing use the policy rates over days / 365. Negotiate sets the lowest complete offer beside the others and asserts no price; with fewer than two rankable complete offers it says it cannot assess. A scenario never changes the forecast and is never ranked.
effect_if_wrong: A different timing or cost rule changes every scenario total.

builder_reading: An opportunity compares a comparable current quote with the last paid order rate for the same material (not an approved baseline), for the quantity not yet ordered. It is always an estimate; claim_saving always refuses.
effect_if_wrong: Using a different reference would change the size of every opportunity; treating it as a saving would overstate.

builder_reading: A cross-project rate comparison is made only when the authorised project set covers every project that bought the material in the window. Each project's weighted average rate is rounded once to cents; the estimate is (higher average - lower average) x the higher project's volume; the gap is relative to the lower average.
effect_if_wrong: A different grouping or rounding changes the gap; reporting with an incomplete set would reveal other projects.

builder_reading: Fill rate is accepted quantity over ordered quantity across the orders that have at least one docket (open orders are not counted as short); acceptance rate is accepted over delivered across dockets that record an accepted quantity. Below a minimum sample the rule says it could not assess. The signal is an observation, not a ranking of suppliers.
effect_if_wrong: Different measures or sample sizes change which supplier is flagged.

builder_reading: The critical checks are a configured list (illustratively customs classification, duty rate confirmed, import permit). A check is resolved only with a status, evidence reference, a named person and a date. Any open critical check keeps a ranking from being definitive. APG states what is unresolved and does not declare a product compliant.
effect_if_wrong: A shorter list would pass an import with open checks.

builder_reading: Each procurement condition writes an apg-event-1 record with event type, observation time, effective time, source provenance, project, material and supplier. Nothing is related, chained or inferred in M6.
effect_if_wrong: Different fields would force rework when the later engine is developed; extra inference would assert a design that has not been agreed.

builder_reading: Every limit, window, tolerance, path and specification in the M6 demonstration policy and register is the builder's illustrative choice. None has product-owner approval.
effect_if_wrong: Treating them as defaults would settle open decisions.

builder_reading: The ranking gate counts offers, not suppliers; a note says when all ranked offers come from one supplier.
effect_if_wrong: Requiring two suppliers would make a one-supplier market never definitive.

topic: Material evidence change that ends an approval
builder_reading: The evidence has changed materially when the signal's state digest differs from the digest the approval names. This is the same test M5 already uses to raise a new finding version. No size threshold is applied, because none has been set; a change that only drifts with time and leaves the digest alone does not end an approval.
effect_if_wrong: A threshold would be a policy decision. Without one, any change to the evidence asks for a fresh approval, which is the safe direction but may ask more often than the business wants.

topic: Approval ended while the action is in progress
builder_reading: When the approval is ended while the finding is in_progress, the finding returns to action_proposed like any other. The record shows that the approval of the old evidence no longer stands. It does not say that work stopped or was undone: APG never carries out an action, so what happens to work already under way is for the people involved.
effect_if_wrong: A separate holding status would be a new lifecycle state, which the auditor directed against. A wrong reading would hide that work had started under an approval that has since ended.

topic: A reopened finding ends the approval it rested on
builder_reading: When a resolved or dismissed finding is reopened by a detection run, an approval still in force is ended in the same step (reason finding_reopened), because the reopened finding is a new version. The finding goes to reopened as before and nothing else changes.
effect_if_wrong: Leaving it in force would let a reopened finding keep a bound approval of a version it no longer is.

topic: Optional version named by the approver
builder_reading: The approval step accepts an optional version number. When it is given and is not the finding's current version the approval is refused (STALE_APPROVAL). When it is not given the approval binds to the version and digest current at that moment. Screens built on the Engine are expected to pass it; that is a handoff point, not something this package can enforce.
effect_if_wrong: Without the version an approver who read an older screen binds an approval to a newer version without having seen it.

topic: The ending of an approval is a service act, not a role transition
builder_reading: The table of allowed transitions is unchanged. Only a detection run, acting as the service, can move an approved or in-progress finding back to action_proposed, and only because the evidence changed. A person still cannot make that move.
effect_if_wrong: Adding it to the table would let a reviewer undo an approval without a cause, which the lifecycle does not allow.

builder_reading: A finding stored before APG-M6.1 has no version or digest on its approval. It is never treated as bound: it does not count as an approval in force, and if its evidence then changes the ending is recorded with no version or digest. No such record exists outside the builder's own tests; moving real data is for the Engine build.
effect_if_wrong: Treating an unbound approval as current would repeat the defect for old data.

topic: A proposal is current only if written against the current version and digest
builder_reading: An action proposal is current when the version and the evidence digest it records equal the finding's present version and digest. Any change of digest makes it stale (the same measure as I-59; no size threshold is applied because none has been set). A proposal with no recorded version or digest (made before M6.1) is never current.
effect_if_wrong: A threshold would be a policy decision. Without one, any change of evidence asks for a fresh proposal, which is the safe direction but may ask more often than the business wants.

topic: A stale proposal is sent back by a reviewer; it is not refreshed in place
builder_reading: A stale proposal cannot be approved and is not silently rewritten to the new evidence. The route is the one the lifecycle already has: a reviewer returns the finding to confirmed with a reason, and the owner proposes the action again. No status and no transition are added; the table of 14 allowed transitions is unchanged.
effect_if_wrong: A direct owner re-proposal or an automatic refresh would be a new transition, which is a lifecycle decision no one has made and the auditor has directed against.

topic: The refusal does not depend on what the approver names
builder_reading: The stale-proposal check runs in the approval step itself. Naming the current version or digest does not make a stale proposal approvable; naming an older one is refused as a stale approval first. The proposer is still refused as a self-approver before anything else.
effect_if_wrong: If the check depended on the optional version, an approver who named nothing, or the current version, would still approve a proposal written against other evidence.

builder_reading: approve_action(scoped, clock, finding, version, digest, rationale) refuses to act unless the version (a whole number of at least 1) and the evidence digest (a non-empty text) are given, and approval_token(finding) gives what a screen must show and hand back. The lower-level transition keeps its optional version for the existing callers. That a screen or API calls approve_action, and passes what it displayed, is a handoff point this package cannot enforce.
effect_if_wrong: Without it an approval screen can approve a version it did not display; with the optional argument alone nothing makes a caller supply it.

topic: What the audit trail keeps when a proposal is replaced or an approval ends
builder_reading: The audit trail keeps the exact action text, who proposed it and when, the finding version and digest it was written against, the approval and its rationale, and what ended it. A replaced proposal is appended to action.proposal_history (with who replaced it and at which version and digest); the proposal and approval events carry the text and the versions; an ended approval keeps the same. Nothing is removed and earlier events are unchanged. Records made before M6.2 lack some of these fields and show them as empty.
effect_if_wrong: If less is needed the extra fields are harmless; if more is needed (for example a rationale for each re-proposal) it is a small addition. Losing the text would leave an approval impossible to reconstruct.

topic: A reopened finding makes its proposal stale
builder_reading: When a resolved or dismissed finding is reopened by a run with changed evidence, an action proposed earlier is marked stale in the same step, as it is for a finding that is simply updated. The finding goes to reopened as before; a reviewer and the owner then follow the same route as for any stale proposal.
effect_if_wrong: Leaving the old proposal current would let a reopened finding carry a proposal for evidence it no longer has.

topic: What counts as a version and as a digest
builder_reading: A version, stored or named, is a whole number of at least 1 and not a boolean; a digest is a non-empty text. The same test applies to the finding's version, the stored proposal version and digest, the approved version and digest, and what an approver names. A malformed stored value means the proposal or approval is not current; a malformed named value is refused as a malformed token (APPROVAL_TOKEN_REQUIRED) before any comparison.
effect_if_wrong: A looser test lets a value that only equals a version under Python's rules stand in for it; a stricter one (for example a format for the digest) would be a further decision.

topic: A proposal marked stale is honoured
builder_reading: A proposal whose record says it is stale is never current, even if its version and digest happen to match the finding. Where no mark exists (records made in M6.1) the version and digest alone decide.
effect_if_wrong: Ignoring the mark would let a damaged or hand-edited record override the run that marked it stale.

builder_reading: The record store refuses floats, so a stored 1.0 cannot be written; it can only reach the check by a direct call. The check refuses it there as well, so the rule does not depend on the store.
effect_if_wrong: Relying on the store alone would leave the function unsafe when used on records from another store.

topic: Damaged records are not repaired in place
builder_reading: The package does not correct a malformed stored value. A proposal that is not current is replaced by the normal route (a reviewer sends it back, the owner proposes again) and the damaged value is kept as found in the proposal history.
effect_if_wrong: Repairing in place would hide the damage; a repair tool for real stored data is for the Engine build.

topic: What makes a proposal "the same" one
builder_reading: A proposal is identified by its exact text, proposer, time, the version and evidence digest it was written against, and the number of proposals it replaced. A proposal written again, even with the same words, is a new proposal and needs a new approval.
effect_if_wrong: A looser reading (the same words are the same proposal) would let an old token approve a re-proposal; a stricter one (a signed proposal) would be an Engine design.

topic: The entry point requires the reference; the lower-level call does not
builder_reading: approve_action, the entry point for screens and APIs, requires the proposal reference and fails closed without it. The lower-level transition keeps its optional arguments for existing callers and checks a reference when one is named. That a screen or API uses approve_action is for the Engine build (CF-22).
effect_if_wrong: Requiring it in the lower-level call as well would change every caller that does not display a proposal, such as the existing lifecycle tests.

builder_reading: An approval stored by M6.1 to M6.3 has no approved_proposal, so approval_current is false for it and a person must approve again. This follows the M6.1 rule for records made before a binding existed.
effect_if_wrong: Treating such an approval as current would trust an approval that cannot be tied to the proposal that was approved; moving stored data is for the Engine build (I-64).

builder_reading: Self-approval, then a malformed named value (APPROVAL_TOKEN_REQUIRED), then an older version or digest (STALE_APPROVAL), then a proposal written against old evidence (STALE_PROPOSAL), then a proposal that is not the one named or cannot be identified (PROPOSAL_CHANGED). The reference is checked after the evidence so the reason given is the first thing that is wrong.
effect_if_wrong: A different order would only change which code a caller sees; every case is refused and audited, and nothing changes in the record.

topic: The approval gate is in the lowest-level call (withdraws the reading I-76)
builder_reading: transition(..., 'action_approved', ...) requires the finding version, the evidence digest and the proposal reference, each well formed, whoever calls it; approve_action is the entry point for screens and APIs and refuses an incomplete token before it looks at the finding at all (so it answers APPROVAL_TOKEN_REQUIRED even for an unknown finding or for the proposer); transition checks the same things after the person and self-approval checks. The reading I-76 (M6.4: the lower-level call keeps its arguments optional for existing callers) was wrong and is withdrawn; I-76 itself is not rewritten because earlier rows are append-only. Existing callers that approve without naming anything are refused; the tests that did so were updated to name what the approver was shown.
effect_if_wrong: Leaving the arguments optional lets any caller of the lower-level function record an approval of something the approver was not shown. A caller that legitimately has no token has no way to approve.

topic: Starting the action re-checks the approval
builder_reading: Moving a finding from action_approved to in_progress requires approval_current to be true for the finding as stored (APPROVAL_NOT_CURRENT otherwise). Through the lifecycle this can only differ from the status when a stored record was changed outside it (a hand edit, a bad migration); detection already returns an approved finding to action_proposed when the evidence changes. It is a second check, not a new rule.
effect_if_wrong: A stricter or looser reading changes only whether a damaged stored record can start work; it does not change what a person can approve. A finding left in action_approved by M6.1 to M6.3 code with an old approval has to be approved again before work starts (I-77).

topic: Input limits of the approval request boundary
builder_reading: A request carries exactly six fields. Identifiers are 1 to 128 characters of letters, digits and . _ : -; the digest and the proposal reference are texts of at most 128 characters; the rationale is a non-empty text of at most 2000 characters. These are bounds on input, chosen so that a request is cheap to check. They are not policy values and nothing in the locked blueprint sets them.
effect_if_wrong: A limit that is too small refuses a legitimate request (a longer rationale); one that is too large lets a request carry more text than anything needs. Either is a one-line change.

topic: The per-action port (EDR-31) is separate from the list of visible projects (EDR-29)
builder_reading: The boundary needs to ask "may this person view / approve in this project", per request. EDR-29 (M6) is the list of projects a caller may see, for a portfolio comparison. They may be answered from one permission table, but they are different questions with different contracts, so the per-action question is a new entry, EDR-31, and EDR-29 is not rewritten. The EDR-29 contract (project_scope_contract, "to be written with M9") is not written in M9.1.
effect_if_wrong: If the Engine decides one operation should serve both, EDR-31 can be folded into EDR-29 or the other way round; the boundary would change in one place.

topic: A finding that does not exist and a finding the person may not approve get the same answer
builder_reading: Every refusal that comes from the finding lookup or the project check is NOT_FOUND, so a person cannot tell a missing finding from one in a project they have no right to. The true reason is written to the audit log, not to the answer.
effect_if_wrong: A distinct "forbidden" answer would tell a person that a finding exists in a project they cannot approve in. A more informative answer could be added for people who may view but not approve; the screen already says can_approve is false.

topic: A replay returns the first answer, not the finding's present state
builder_reading: Sending the same request again returns the answer the request id first got (marked replayed), even if the approval has since ended because the evidence changed. Only the execution-time check says whether an approval is in force now. The port is still asked on every replay, so a person whose permission was taken away is not served the old answer.
effect_if_wrong: A replay that reported the present state would not be a repeat of the first answer. Someone who reads a replayed "approved" as "still in force" would be wrong; the documents say so.

topic: Refusals before a request record is opened are not replayed
builder_reading: A request that is malformed, from a service identity, from an ended session, from someone without the approver role, or for a finding the person may not approve in is refused and audited each time, but nothing is stored under its request id; the id is "used" only once the person has passed those checks. The lifecycle's own refusals (stale, replaced proposal, self-approval) are stored as the answer to the id.
effect_if_wrong: Storing every refusal would let any caller fill the request store with ids it cannot use for anything; storing none would let a refused id be re-used with different content. The first is the choice made here.

topic: The execution-time check is open to anyone who may view the finding
builder_reading: check_for_execution does not need the approver role: it reports whether an approval is in force, to whoever carries the action out, provided the port says that person may view the finding. It is audited. It is advisory: APG executes nothing and nothing in APG calls it.
effect_if_wrong: If only approvers or a dedicated execution right should be able to ask, the port would need a third action and the Engine would decide who holds it.

topic: A half-finished request is credited with an approval only if its own history shows it
builder_reading: If a request stopped between the approval and the note of it, the next try recognises the approval from the finding's own history, but only an approval written after the request was opened, by the same person, of exactly the same version, digest and proposal. An earlier approval, or one made by another request, is not credited; the request is then refused by the lifecycle like any other.
effect_if_wrong: A looser rule could report "approved" for a request that approved nothing; a stricter one would approve a second time after a crash. The first is the error to avoid.

topic: The approval token goes only to a caller who can approve now
builder_reading: M9.1 read "the token is given only for a finding that can be approved now" as a property of the finding. M9.2 reads it as a property of the caller as well: the token is returned only when can_approve is true (the proposal is current and not yet approved, the caller has the approver role, is not the proposer, and the port allows approve in the finding's project). A caller who may only view still sees the proposal and the status, and can_approve false. This withdraws the M9.1 reading without rewriting it.
effect_if_wrong: If a viewer should be able to hand a token to someone else (for example to paste into a ticket), the token would have to be requested separately; nothing in the lifecycle needs that. The effect of the old reading was to disclose the version, digest and proposal reference to a viewer.

topic: The approval's audit entry is written before the answer is noted, so the audit is at least once
builder_reading: In M9.1 the answer was noted under the request id first and audited second. If the audit entry failed, the retry returned the noted answer as a replay and the entry never existed. M9.2 writes the entry first and unprotected: if it fails the call raises, the answer is not noted, and the retry recognises the approval from the finding's history and writes the entry. A crash between the entry and the note can leave two entries for one approval; the second says it was recovered. Exactly-once needs the Engine (EDR-32).
effect_if_wrong: A reader who counts accepted entries as approvals would over-count after such a crash; the entries carry the request id and the finding, so duplicates are recognisable. Exactly-once would need a transaction across the state change and the log.

topic: A conflict on opening the request record is audited as a refusal with the code CONCURRENT_CHANGE
builder_reading: No new event type was added: the outcome is written as approval_request.refused with the code CONCURRENT_CHANGE in the detail, as the other transient outcome already was. It is best-effort like every refusal.
effect_if_wrong: If the Engine wants transient outcomes under their own event type, it is a one-line change in the boundary and in the contract document.

topic: Identifiers and the session expiry time are matched as whole strings of ASCII characters
builder_reading: An identifier is 1 to 128 characters of ASCII letters, digits and . _ : - and nothing else, so a final newline, a space, a control character or a non-ASCII digit makes the request malformed. The session expiry must be exactly YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ in ASCII digits, otherwise the session is not live.
effect_if_wrong: A looser rule lets a control character reach the audit log or a comparison; a stricter one (for example refusing a colon) would refuse identifiers the Engine may use. The pattern is one line.

topic: A refused call of the executor check is audited best-effort
builder_reading: check_for_execution now writes an audit event for a malformed call or an ended session as it already did for the other refusals. A session that no longer verifies cannot write to the tenant's log; the answer (NOT_ALLOWED) stands and nothing is raised.
effect_if_wrong: If every refusal must be recorded even when the session cannot write, the Engine needs a system-level log for it; that is not designed here.

topic: A session expiry is live only if it is a real UTC moment strictly later than now
builder_reading: The expiry must be exactly YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ in ASCII digits AND a moment that exists: month 1 to 12, a day the month has in that year (29 February only in a Gregorian leap year: divisible by 4, not by 100 unless by 400), hour 0 to 23, minute 0 to 59, second 0 to 59. It is live only if it is strictly later than the present time; an expiry equal to now has ended. Nothing else (a zone offset, fractional seconds, a lower-case letter) is a moment.
effect_if_wrong: If the Engine issues expiries in another format (an offset, fractional seconds) every session would be refused until the format or this rule is agreed: a fail-closed effect, visible at once. If an expiry equal to now should still be live, one comparison changes.

topic: A leap second and the year 0000 are not accepted
builder_reading: Second 60 is refused, and so is year 0000; years run 0001 to 9999. This is stricter than ISO 8601, which allows a leap second in some timescales, and matches what most programming-language date types accept. A session that lasts into a leap second simply ends one second earlier in the worst case.
effect_if_wrong: If the Engine's clock can emit second 60, sessions in that second would be refused (fail closed); the table of accepted ranges is one line.

topic: A clock that does not give a real moment ends every session
builder_reading: The present time comes from the clock the caller supplies. If it is not itself a real UTC moment in the same format, no session is live (fail closed) rather than comparing an expiry with a meaningless string. The real clock and its format are the Engine's.
effect_if_wrong: If a deployment's clock uses another format the boundary would refuse everything until they agree; it would not approve anything wrongly.

topic: A clock or expiry that cannot be read ends the session as an ordinary refusal
builder_reading: If clock.now() raises an ordinary exception, the clock is missing or not callable, or the context's expiry (or actor kind) cannot be read, the session is treated as ended. The call gives the refusal it already gives for an ended session (present: NOT_ALLOWED; request_approval: SESSION_EXPIRED, or HUMAN_REQUIRED for an actor kind that cannot be read; check_for_execution: valid False, NOT_ALLOWED). No new result code is added. The refusal is audited best-effort like every refusal, with a reason that says the clock gave no usable time; the text of the exception is not copied into the audit trail.
effect_if_wrong: If the API layer wants a distinct code for an unavailable clock (for example a retryable error), one code is added at the Engine's mapping; until then the caller sees an ended session and signs in again.

topic: The clock is read once per call and that reading is the time of the call
builder_reading: The boundary reads the clock once, at the session check. The lifecycle and the boundary then use that one reading for every timestamp of the call, so the session check and the approval carry the same instant and a clock that fails after its first read cannot stop an approval half way. A clock that moves on during one call is therefore read once rather than at each write.
effect_if_wrong: If a caller needs each write stamped at its own moment, the stamps would be equal within one call; the audit log has its own times. Reverting means reading the clock again inside the lifecycle and guarding every read.

topic: Only ordinary exceptions are a refusal; other context attributes are the Engine's
builder_reading: The guard catches ordinary exceptions (Exception). An interrupt (KeyboardInterrupt, SystemExit) is not caught. The attributes the boundary reads to decide the session (the clock, the expiry, the actor kind) are guarded; the others (tenant, user, roles, session id, seal) belong to the Engine's sealed context and are read as before.
effect_if_wrong: If the Engine's context can raise when its other attributes are read, those calls would still raise; the Engine's context contract should say whether they may.

builder_reading: Every item of missing information a finding lists is treated as critical until a constraint reviewer records, with a reason, that it is not critical for acting. Unresolved critical evidence routes the finding to investigate (never to a ready action).
effect_if_wrong: If the product owner wants some items to be non-critical by rule, the reviewer step is extra work; nothing unsafe follows.

builder_reading: Urgency is how soon the dated condition falls due (overdue, soon within the policy days, later, not dated); time sensitivity is whether a decision window closes. For an opportunity a closed window ends the opportunity (route close); for an exposure a passed date means the matter is overdue (state passed, ranked with closing windows). The signal carries one date, so the two dimensions use the same date in different ways.
effect_if_wrong: A separate deterioration measure may be wanted; the signal contract of M5 would need it.

builder_reading: The ranking is lexicographic in the order the policy names; there are no weights and no combined score. The deciding dimension and both values are stated for every line; a full tie is broken by finding id and says so.
effect_if_wrong: If weights are wanted, the explanation would need the contribution of each factor; a policy change, not a code change of the lifecycle.

builder_reading: A net benefit is stated only from an expected benefit and every incremental cost that a person entered, each with a basis. The finding amount (exposure or opportunity) is shown as potential gross, never as a benefit.
effect_if_wrong: None for safety; the owner must enter the figures for every action.

builder_reading: Inside an overlap component (the M5 rule: same overlap group, a shared stored record, or a person's financial_overlap link) only the recommendation with the largest potential gross is counted in the totals; the others are listed as overlapping. Totals are per interpretation and never added across interpretations.
effect_if_wrong: The counted amount is a lower bound of the component, as in the M5 portfolio view.

builder_reading: The approval role comes from policy bands on the absolute potential gross amount; an unquantified recommendation needs the highest band, because nothing shows it is small.
effect_if_wrong: The product owner may prefer bands on net benefit or on the commitment value.

builder_reading: A baseline for verification is an M4 forecast calculation that a forecast owner adopted (or explicitly promoted) in a forecast slot, that still replays, and that was adopted no later than the time the action was started.
effect_if_wrong: Some benefit types may need another baseline kind (a procurement baseline, an approved rate); the gate would accept more kinds by a change.

topic: Evidence changing while an action is in progress
builder_reading: People are already acting outside APG, which APG cannot stop: the status stays in progress, the approval is ended and the event is recorded and visible.
effect_if_wrong: The product owner may want such a recommendation to move back to awaiting approval; the M5 finding lifecycle does that for findings.

builder_reading: Route close (a resolved finding, an expired opportunity) is a recommendation to close; a person records the closure with a reason. No service closes a recommendation.
effect_if_wrong: None for safety.

builder_reading: A decision is material when the potential gross reaches the policy amount; without that amount every action is treated as material. A material decision needs at least one complete alternative (all nine Section 10 section 7 items) beside the engine-generated no-action reference, and every alternative names a stored forecast calculation as its reference baseline.
effect_if_wrong: A lower bar would let more recommendations through without a comparison.

builder_reading: M5 findings carry their own action approval (findings.approve_action, the M9 boundary); M7 recommendations carry theirs. M7 does not change the finding lifecycle: a finding whose action is already approved or in progress is tracked, not recommended again. Whether the two approvals should become one is for the product owner.
effect_if_wrong: Duplicate approvals for one action until the product owner decides.

topic: What counts as a changed source
builder_reading: Any new revision of the finding, an overlapping finding, the recommendation inputs or the policy refuses submission, approval and start, even when nothing material changed (for example a detection sweep that only refreshes when the finding was last seen). A fresh run then either keeps the version (the submission or approval stands) or makes a new one. This is fail-closed and asks for more runs.
effect_if_wrong: If refusing after every detection sweep is too strict, the exact check could ignore the fields detection refreshes; the recomputation would still catch material changes.

topic: Completion and verification are not source-checked
builder_reading: After people have started the work, a source change is recorded and ends the approval (I-106) but does not stop completion or verification: they record what happened, and the verifier sees the history.
effect_if_wrong: If the product owner wants completion blocked after a source change, add in_progress -> completed to the checked moves.

builder_reading: A policy approval counts only when the tenant's audit log holds a rec.policy_approved event for that version written under the approver's own verified human context. APG cannot stop code outside its functions from writing the store or the audit log directly; restricting who may write these record kinds is the Engine's (EDR-34).
effect_if_wrong: With an Engine that lets any caller write the policy record kind and the audit log under their own name, a person could still approve as themselves without the role check.

builder_reading: Recommendations computed under a policy that no policy owner has approved (as confirmed by the audit log) are shown and ranked but cannot be submitted for approval.
effect_if_wrong: If the product owner wants unapproved policies usable in a pilot, this gate would need a recorded exception.

builder_reading: Every stored record the check read is held, not only the ones pinned for this recommendation: the recomputation reads every finding and every set of recommendation inputs in the tenant, and any of them can change its result. So a change anywhere in those records during the act refuses it. If the sources of this recommendation still match, the refusal is CONCURRENT_CHANGE and trying again is enough; otherwise it is SOURCE_CHANGED and the engine must run again.
effect_if_wrong: If refusals from unrelated concurrent changes are too frequent in practice, the guard could be narrowed to the records the recomputation of this recommendation depends on.

topic: A record created during the act
builder_reading: The store contract can hold an existing record at a revision but cannot hold a record as absent, or a query as unchanged, without writing. A record created between the check and the write (a new overlapping finding, say) is therefore caught by running the check again once the act is recorded; if it now fails, the act is reversed at once with an audited, append-only reversal, and refused. For that moment the stored record shows the act. Every act that could follow from it (approval after a submission, the start of work after an approval) is itself source-checked and refused.
effect_if_wrong: If even a reversed, momentary record of the act is not acceptable, the Engine store must provide absence or query guards, or serialisable transactions (EDR-35).

topic: When a checked act takes effect, and what counts as a later change
builder_reading: A checked act takes effect at the moment its store batch commits, and only if every guard holds then: the sources are exactly those it was checked against. A record committed before that moment refuses the act and nothing is recorded. A record committed after it is a later change, ordered after the act in the store, and is handled like any later change: the next checked act is refused and the next run ends a submission or approval that no longer matches. This includes a record created after the commit but before the call returns. I-115 no longer applies: there is no check after the commit and no reversal.
effect_if_wrong: If the product owner wants no overlapping finding to be creatable at all while an act is in progress, detection writes and the acts would need a shared lock or a common guarded record; that changes M5 and is a decision for the product owner.

topic: M7.3 changes the shared record store
builder_reading: The race could only be closed at the store, so M7.3 changes M2 files: the port contract (apg/ports.py: Guard and the atomic batch), the reference store (apg/reference_impl.py: guards and a lock) and the scoped store (apg/tenancy.py: guards passed on, query filters screened). The change is additive: a batch without guards behaves exactly as before, the 38 M2 contract cases and the 39 faulty implementations give the same results, and every earlier test passes unchanged.
effect_if_wrong: If the M2 port contract must not change outside an M2 release, the guard contract (EDR-36) would move to its own release and M7.3 would wait for it.

builder_reading: The core is an in-process library: the host constructs the Engine with its own implementations of the outbound ports (context, stores, audit append and query, approvals, hooks, limits). The core reads nothing else. mie/core/reference.py holds non-production in-memory ports for tests; mie/adapters/apg_host.py lets APG's verified context be the core's tenant context.
effect_if_wrong: If the core must run as a separate service, the twelve operations need a transport and the ports a remote form; the core logic is unchanged.

topic: Who can see, withdraw and activate a pack
builder_reading: The pack registry is platform-wide: any verified tenant may read a registered pack by its exact pin. Activation is per tenant and needs an approval reference that the ApprovalVerifierPort verifies for that tenant and that exact pin; an approver who is the pack's author is refused. Only the publishing tenant can withdraw a pack; to any other tenant a withdrawal attempt looks like a missing pack (NOT_FOUND).
effect_if_wrong: If packs must be private to a tenant, get_pack and register_pack would be scoped by tenant; the tests in test_mie_core_pack.py would change.

topic: PACK_INCOMPLETE and NOT_FOUND for a subject the pack does not declare
builder_reading: assess_timing (OP-09) refuses a subject the active pack does not declare with PACK_INCOMPLETE: the pack cannot yet assess it. get_signals (OP-08) refuses it with NOT_FOUND, because its error list has no PACK_INCOMPLETE.
effect_if_wrong: If an undeclared subject should be NOT_ASSESSED with a gap rather than refused, both operations change and AU-11 would be re-run.

builder_reading: Derived by reading M6 and M3 source, read only: market_observation material_ref, obs_date, value_scaled (kept exactly as {mantissa, exponent 0} in its stored unit), unit_text, kind_text (index -> HISTORICAL_MOVEMENT, INDEX), source_label_text, geography_text and provenance.received_at map to subject, as_of, value, unit, class and basis, source, market and retrieved_at; fx_rate maps to the subject FX:<pair> with the rate parsed exactly from its decimal text, class CURRENT_REFERENCE. Records M4 or M6 would not use are not submitted and are reported; a conflict marker is submitted as each contender so that the core reports the conflict.
effect_if_wrong: If the review of the mapping finds a different reading (for example of the index unit or the FX class), only the adapter and the pack inputs change; the core does not.

builder_reading: PSA02-D2 (specification_ref and methodology_ref and their mismatch rejection), DECLARATION_CHANGED with re-attestation, and the P1 normal form are not implemented: each rests on a decision that is still open. No placeholder code stands in for them.
effect_if_wrong: If any is decided, it is a later, separately authorised change to the pack schema, the observation schema or both.

topic: Evidence that counts as usable for a subject
builder_reading: A subject's usable evidence includes the series of the conversions the pack declares for it. So a material with no index evidence of its own but a current conversion series is assessed (not NOT_ASSESSED for NO_EVIDENCE), and the result is QUALIFIED with the missing required evidence listed. In the Builder Zero run this is MAT-PBOARD: a CONTEXT_ONLY date rule fires (ACT_NOW, influence NONE) while its own index evidence is NO_EVIDENCE.
effect_if_wrong: If only the subject's own series should count, signals.assess_evidence would count usable evidence for the subject alone and MAT-PBOARD would be NOT_ASSESSED with NO_EVIDENCE; the golden file would change.

topic: The retrieval date of an observation from the M6 feed
builder_reading: The M6 MarketFeedPort reports no retrieval date for an observation, so the M6 feed adapter asserts one from the integrator's clock (an adapter-side callable). The core checks only that it is not earlier than as_of (MIE-L-18).
effect_if_wrong: If a retrieval date must come from the feed, the M6 port would need a field, which is an M6 change and not made here.

builder_reading: A correction (an observation naming another in supersedes) is valid only for an observation of the same series (subject, market, unit, observation class, value basis), from the same source, for the same as_of date, and of the same kind (both a LEVEL value or both an EVENT). This reads section 4.7 ("for one series and as_of") strictly. A changed date or source is a new observation, not a correction.
effect_if_wrong: If a correction may change its as_of date or its source, signals.corrects would allow it; the correction tests would change.

topic: What fails closed at the commit and at the audit sink
builder_reading: An audit sink that raises anything is unavailable: AUDIT_UNAVAILABLE, nothing proceeds. A store that raises StoreFailure at the commit is STORE_UNAVAILABLE; any other exception there is INTERNAL_ERROR_FAIL_CLOSED. In both, one FAILED event is attempted after the ACCEPTED event, and no result is returned. Whether the ACCEPTED event and the commit are atomic remains the host's (BLK-01).
effect_if_wrong: If an unexpected store exception should be reported as STORE_UNAVAILABLE, the engine would map it so; the outcome stays fail-closed.
